courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Landscape Architecture
courses.description: This course examines emerging issues within landscape architecture, exploring its potential capacity to understand, critique and imagine our increasingly complex human-environmental systems in the face of contemporary global problems such as climate change, biodiversity, environmental and spatial injustice, etc. Through seminars, case studies and guest talks, this course interrogates current issues of landscape research, sustainable design and practice through selected themes - (e.g.. historic and cultural landscapes, border/edge conditions, urban-rural interfaces, land-water ecologies, etc.)
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture, MSc in Urban Design and MArch.
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion of the course, students will have acquired a deeper understanding of current issues and debates in a specific area of landscape architecture. Students will also gain an understanding of the relevance of the topic to contemporary design practice and research.
courses.course_syllabus: Topics in this course refer to contemporary issues in landscape research and practice.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Computational Techniques in Landscape Design
courses.description: This course explores the latest advances in computational tools for landscape architecture that is able to document, analyse and simulate landscapes to high levels of precision through the generation of 3D digital models from various two-dimensional data accessible (ecological, social, topographical, etc). Students will be introduced to GIS spatial analysis, digital information modelling and simulations that relate to contemporary landscape design practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Demonstrate familiarity with contemporary computational tools and techniques relevant to landscape architecture practice.

2. Understand the role of digital technologies in landscape analysis, documentation, and design development.

3. Apply computational methods to support design inquiry and decision-making.
courses.course_syllabus: The core content / syllabus should be covered by the course and selected topics may be added by any individual course instructor. Topics in this course will refer to issues in landscape design, theory, and practice methods framed by technology adoption, exploration, and virtuosity.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Landscape Technology and Construction
courses.description: This course consists of two parts. The first part explores how modern technology transforms perception, experience and understanding of built landscapes and natural environments, and covers relevant technological knowledge and skills in site analysis and planning. Geographic Information System (GIS) is provided as an essential tool for mapping, analysing, managing and modelling relevant landscape data. The second part focuses on landscape engineering aspects. Site engineering topics will include site investigation, earthworks, grading, drainage, basic surveying, etc., while principles and technologies of sustainable landscape design such as hydrology and hydraulics fundamentals, storm water management, bioretention systems and constructed wetland construction will be introduced.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Apply advanced technological tools to analyze and represent landscape conditions and processes.

2. Integrate site engineering principles into landscape design proposals.

3. Demonstrate technical competency in grading, drainage, and sustainable landscape construction methods.

4. Utilize GIS and other digital tools for data-driven landscape analysis and design decision-making.
courses.course_syllabus: The course combines lectures on theoretical principles with hands-on workshops and technical exercises. Topics include GIS applications, site engineering fundamentals, sustainable construction technologies, and documentation methods. Students will apply these skills through practical exercises and technical studies.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio III
courses.description: The third studio course further develops students’ ability to research, analyse, conceptualise and create substantial landscape designs that articulate rigorous, organised and critical design positions. Students will practice more advanced analytical and representational techniques, including analogue and digital modelling and simulation of landscape processes (eg. GIS, BIM, etc). Coursework may be conducted in relation to real-life projects (urban or rural landscape sites) to offer students first-hand design-research and material fabrication experience. Thesis Studio is self-directed, and the topic of the thesis project is expected to be preliminarily developed in discussion with instructors in this course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Independently formulate a design research inquiry that addresses complex environmental and social challenges at multiple scales.

2. Develop advanced analytical and representational skills using digital and analogue tools to communicate landscape processes and design interventions.

3. Demonstrate critical thinking in defining a design position that integrates the program's pillars of Nature, Ecology, and People.

4. Synthesize knowledge from previous coursework to frame an original thesis project with clear objectives and methodology.
courses.course_syllabus: The studio operates through individual consultations, group discussions, and iterative design development. Students will identify a thesis topic, conduct preliminary research, develop analytical frameworks, and establish a clear design methodology. The course includes workshops on advanced representation techniques and research methods.
courses.feedback_evaluation:
1. Weekly desk critiques.

2 Iterative feedback from specialist consultants on technical aspects of the design.

3. Formal final review with all collaborating project partners.

4. External examiner reports.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio IV Thesis
courses.description: The concluding studio comprises an integrated design thesis project elaborated from topics defined in LARC6111. As a capstone project, students are expected to develop their sustainable design thesis through in-depth research and analysis to synthesise accomplished landscape proposals that address multi-faceted concerns (ecological, social, political, economic) through multi-scalar designs (from regional strategy to local interventions). Self-directed thesis projects should explore innovative topics (eg. regenerative design, biophilia, nature-based low-carbon solutions, environmental justice, etc.), and aspire to resolving technically complex sustainable landscape designs that balance human needs while enhancing urban-rural landscape systems and ecological processes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Execute a comprehensive, self-directed design thesis that demonstrates mastery of landscape architectural thinking and design skills.

2. Integrate advanced technical knowledge, ecological science, and social considerations into a cohesive and innovative design proposal.

3. Articulate design decisions through high-quality documentation including drawings, models, diagrams, and written analysis.

4. Defend their design position and methodology through rigorous critique and professional presentation.

5. Demonstrate readiness for professional practice and leadership in addressing complex landscape challenges.
courses.course_syllabus: The thesis studio is structured around independent work with regular faculty consultation. Students will refine their design proposals, develop detailed documentation, and prepare comprehensive presentations. The process culminates in a public thesis defense and exhibition showcasing the final work.
courses.feedback_evaluation:
1. Weekly desk critiques.

2. Iterative feedback from specialist consultants on technical aspects of the design.

3. Formal final review with all collaborating project partners.

4. External examiner reports.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

courses.subject: LARC
courses.title: Professional Practice and Management in Landscape Architecture
courses.description: This course introduces students to the professional practice of landscape architecture. Regulatory control mechanisms and significant procedures for land use, planning and design development in Hong Kong will be discussed. Codes of professional conduct, nature of scope of services, project team members and roles, project management practices and will be presented. Tender documents, specifications and construction contracts, as well as the administration process for implementation of landscape works will be discussed; while related legal aspects in the Laws of Tort; Contract; Land; and Environment will be mentioned. In addition, the course covers professional presentations and communication with client and user communities while advocating for values of diversity of sustainable design practices and environmental stewardship in compliance with UN SDGs.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:

1. Understand the regulatory framework governing landscape architecture practice in Hong Kong and internationally.

2. Demonstrate knowledge of professional ethics, codes of conduct, and scope of services.

3. Understand the principles of project management, contract administration, and professional documentation in landscape architecture practice.

4. Communicate effectively with clients, stakeholders, and project teams while advocating for sustainable design values.
courses.course_syllabus: The course combines lectures, case studies, and practical exercises covering professional practice topics. Guest speakers from practice and regulatory bodies will share insights. Topics include regulatory processes, project delivery methods, contract administration, legal considerations, and professional communication strategies.
courses.required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.
